scope: Observable main-chat contracts apply to every agent; missing evidence is a failure, never a policy exemption. Fixture evidence is not live/browser evidence.

derivation.method: main branch source, server test inventory, UX tests/browser suites, merge/commit subjects and loaded chat/release skills

policies.rule: Private agent only, by owner decision: each standard runtime must refuse Incognito before upstream admission.

Owner-scoped hermes-only: James explicitly requested 'Archimedes only' on 27 Oct 2026 for owned-open-work follow-through. Routed instructions, status projection and admissions remain untouched; this does not exempt any other chat feature.
Private agent history, memory and home are invisible to standard agents. Do not test against existing private agents; use fresh disposable synthetic data.
Agent model allowlists and restricted-provider unsupported combinations remain enforced; test an allowed model, never exempt the whole model picker.
An explicit files:none grant refuses attachments; files:own must support attached bytes. Do not count unavailable placement as policy.
Restricted runtime must use its per-agent Unix socket and edge transport; no host TCP fallback.

features.description: A new chat starts even when another, optional agent on the box is registered as running but cannot be reached: the anti-claim scan skips a standard (non-private) agent that cannot answer for a fresh client-minted id (wizard_<ms>_<12 hex>) that no agent was ever pinned to; ids an agent is known to hold (pin or session catalog), any unreachable private agent and arbitrary ids still fail closed.
features.how_to_test: With a second registered agent whose upstream refuses connections (no sealed catalog), through each main, host-profile, container and restricted agent's own Service route: POST /api/sessions with a fresh wizard_<ms>_<12 hex> id returns 201 on that runtime and a first /v1/runs send for another fresh id returns 202; an arbitrary non-fresh id still returns 503 agent_unavailable; on main, the same new chat without an agent name also lands on the default agent. tests/round2-boundaries.test.ts covers pinned ids of the unreachable agent (still refused: 503 by id, 409 thread_agent_pinned for a claim) an answering agent behind the unreachable one still colliding, and an unreachable private agent still failing closed (503). Synthetic HTTP fixture evidence, not live box proof.

features.description: The wizard MCP gateway's tools/list carries SEP-2549 cache hints (ttlMs, cacheScope private) so a caching client such as Hermes lazy: true can register app tools at chat start; only a complete discovery is cacheable (one day), and any visible app that is stopped, failing, malformed, filtered, paginated or replaced during the request makes the reply ttlMs 0.
features.how_to_test: Through each main, host-profile, container and restricted agent's own gateway credential and transport (restricted: Unix socket), install a synthetic answering MCP app and call tools/list: its tool is listed with ttlMs 86400000 and cacheScope private. Add a second visible app that cannot be reached: the answering app's tool is still listed and ttlMs is 0. tests/agent-bridge-cache.node.mjs covers failure, cached retry, recovery, empty/malformed/paginated/filtered discovery, stopped apps and grant or registry changes during discovery through the production gateway with a synthetic transport. Not stock Hermes cache registration or reconnect.

features.description: Scoped chat media opens the shared viewer: desktop images fit the viewport, Left/Right navigate in order, close restores the exact thread and draft, and phone open/Back remains scoped after cold selected-agent restore.
features.how_to_test: Run QA_GROUP=media QA_KINDS=main,host-profile,container,restricted QA_UX_ROOT=<ux> QA_OUT=<fresh-output> QA_EXTERNAL_ROOT=<worker-root> node qa/agent-parity/browser.mjs on the admitted browser worker. Linux additionally requires QA_FORUM_MEDIA=1 QA_CHROMIUM=<pinned-chrome> QA_PLAYWRIGHT=<pinned-playwright>. This narrow cell clicks actual rendered MEDIA buttons from synthetic transcripts through the real Service; host-profile really traverses /p/<profile>, container uses a distinct TCP origin, restricted uses mode-0600 Unix ingress. Browser and disposable runtime reject mutations after seed; no real agents/providers/private history are opened. Desktop fit at two widths, ordered trusted Left/Right, focus, Escape/outside and phone open/Back/outside preserve cold-selected agent/thread/draft. Native video/audio UA seeking is separately covered by wizard-ux/qa-viewer-desktop-fit.cjs with mandatory provisioned QA_MEDIA_DIR. Synthetic-runtime browser evidence is not real-container/provider/physical-device acceptance. Companion UX PRs #1039/#1038.

features.description: Controller and live-lease execution outrank out-of-band notice attention while queued or steered owner messages arrive; notices can classify Ready only after the run ends.
features.how_to_test: Exercise full and slim HTTP lists for main, host-profile, container and restricted Unix ingress, with an admitted synthetic run, heavy background work, needs_you notice, owner message queued outside history then persisted steer, another notice and a real terminal receipt. No live owner writes, provider or browser proof.

features.description: Owner text, recording chips and inline multipart media survive history projection when Hermes coalesces them after a helper completion, before the matching reply; helper material stays hidden.
features.how_to_test: Read synthetic coalesced history through each runtime's actual Service HTTP route (main, host-profile, container and restricted Unix ingress); require original row/client identity, time, text, recording and inline media, unchanged upstream rows, and no admitted run. Synthetic routed HTTP evidence, not live/provider/browser or physical phone proof.

features.description: The owner's own messages stay visible in chat history when Hermes 0.22.7 stamps the admitted user row internal_notification: each kind restores the turn from its own run queue (routed kinds behind WIZARD_ROUTED_OWNER_TURNS=1, off by default), once, while machine wakes with the same kind stay hidden.
features.how_to_test: Through each runtime's actual Service HTTP route (main, host-profile /p/<profile>, container TCP, restricted Unix ingress) with routedOwnerTurns on: admit a list-shaped synthetic owner turn, stamp its upstream row internal_notification, add a [Wizard follow-through] wake with the same kind, then read ?view=wizard history. Require the owner row exactly once as a normal user row, the wake still internal, upstream rows and raw history unchanged. tests/routed-owner-turns.test.ts proves routed kinds are unchanged with the switch off. Synthetic HTTP fixture evidence, not live/provider/browser proof.

features.description: The owner's own message with an inline screenshot stays visible when Hermes stores it as its words plus "[screenshot]" and stamps it internal_notification: each kind matches the queued multipart turn by its screenshot-marked text (behind WIZARD_OWNER_SCREENSHOT_TURNS=1, off by default; routed kinds also need WIZARD_ROUTED_OWNER_TURNS=1).
features.how_to_test: Through each runtime's actual Service HTTP route (main, host-profile /p/<profile>, container TCP, restricted Unix ingress) with routedOwnerTurns and ownerScreenshotTurns on: admit a synthetic owner turn with text and an inline PNG, store its upstream row as the words plus [screenshot] stamped internal_notification, add a [Wizard follow-through] wake, then read ?view=wizard history. Require the owner row exactly once as a normal user row, the wake still internal and upstream rows unchanged. tests/owner-screenshot-turns.test.ts covers screenshot-only rows, missing rows, whitespace and the switch off. Synthetic HTTP fixture evidence, not live/provider/browser proof.

features.description: Retry rebuilds the owner's own latest message when Hermes 0.22.5+ stamped its row internal_notification: the detail view's wizard_retry_input reads history with the owner's turns restored from this kind's own queue (behind WIZARD_OWNER_TURN_RETRY=1, off by default; routed kinds also need WIZARD_ROUTED_OWNER_TURNS=1).
features.how_to_test: Through each runtime's actual Service HTTP route (main, host-profile /p/<profile>, container TCP, restricted Unix ingress) with routedOwnerTurns and ownerTurnRetry on: admit a list-shaped synthetic owner turn, stamp its upstream row internal_notification, finish the run, then read GET /api/sessions/wizard_parity?view=detail. Require wizard_retry_input to equal the owner's words. tests/owner-turn-followups.test.ts shows the plain scan skipping the row and Hermes' [System:] notice being dropped. Synthetic HTTP fixture evidence, not live/provider/browser proof.

features.description: A finished owner send keeps its words (never its image bytes) in a small per-queue ledger when retention prunes it after 7 days / 128 runs, so the owner's internal_notification row is still restored on every kind (behind WIZARD_OWNER_TURN_LEDGER=1, off by default; routed kinds also need WIZARD_ROUTED_OWNER_TURNS=1).
features.how_to_test: Through each runtime's actual Service HTTP route (main, host-profile /p/<profile>, container TCP, restricted Unix ingress) with routedOwnerTurns and ownerTurnLedger on: admit a list-shaped synthetic owner turn, stamp its upstream row internal_notification, age it past retention with 130 synthetic filler runs and force retention through a second DurableRunQueue handle on that kind's own queue file, then read ?view=wizard history. Require the owner row exactly once as a normal user row. tests/owner-turn-followups.test.ts covers image stripping, service sends never kept, restart and the switch off. Synthetic HTTP fixture evidence, not live/provider/browser proof.

features.description: A send the Service queued itself (heavy-work continuation, follow-through, helper receipt: continuation metadata or their idempotency keys, or a machine-tagged input) is never matched or restored as the owner's own message, whatever shape its input has. Plain fix, on for main; routed kinds follow WIZARD_ROUTED_OWNER_TURNS=1.
features.how_to_test: Through each runtime's actual Service HTTP route (main, host-profile /p/<profile>, container TCP, restricted Unix ingress) with routedOwnerTurns on: queue a list-shaped synthetic send keyed wizard-heavy-* with heavy continuation metadata on that kind's own queue, store its Hermes row with the same words stamped internal_notification, then read ?view=wizard history. Require the row to stay internal and no queue copy to be added. tests/owner-turn-followups.test.ts covers continuation metadata, the heavy key and machine-tagged text. Synthetic HTTP fixture evidence, not live/provider/browser proof.

features.description: Reopening the shell short-answer view accepts and persists its existing box-wide choice while main, host-profile, container and restricted chats retain their own unchanged transcripts and admit no reply.
features.how_to_test: For each runtime kind, read its real routed transcript (host-profile via its profile API, restricted via mode-0600 Unix ingress), then GET/PUT the shell's owner-level /wizard/v1/ui-preferences route. Require absent-stays-absent, successful existing reopen payload, exact preservation of unrelated/future stored fields, restart readback, atomic invalid-field rejection, unchanged transcript and zero admitted replies. Synthetic HTTP fixture evidence only, not live runtime, browser or physical-phone proof.

features.description: While the owner's short-answer view is on (ui-preferences replySummary.on), its length line/sentences/paragraph sets the status ask budget to 80/140/300 characters in the instructions sent to main, host-profile, container and restricted runtimes; off or absent keeps 140.
features.how_to_test: For each runtime kind, store replySummary absent, on+line, on+sentences, on+paragraph and off+paragraph in the box ui-preferences, admit a run through the kind's real ingress, and require the forwarded upstream instructions to carry exactly the 140/80/140/300/140-character ask rule and no other. Synthetic HTTP fixture evidence only, not live model output.

features.description: An admitted installed app opens the shared native thread with exact owner text held as a draft, not a send; app context remains quoted data and hosted audio stays bound to its original thread, model and run.
features.how_to_test: In wizard-ux run node --test tests/hosted-thread-routes.test.mjs tests/thread-draft-admission.test.mjs tests/hosted-reply-recorder.test.mjs. Source-executed main, host-profile, container and restricted UX fixtures run the real App Services admission, openHosted and durable draft store; verify exact text/reload, conflict refusal before agent pinning, quoted reply context, hidden/revoked source refusal, and recorder retry custody with the same scoped thread/model/run/id. The recorder's Chats delivery boundary is instrumented, not a real Service/runtime transport. No browser, HTTP runtime, provider or physical microphone acceptance is earned. Companion UX PR #920.

features.description: Owner-level installed app Ready cards are independent of agent threads: they render/poll only at the owner root, never inside main-session, host-profile, container or restricted-agent contexts; writes require the actual shell-owned app frame.
features.how_to_test: Run wizard-ux/tests/app-ready-extension.test.mjs: compare root versus synthetic host-profile/container/restricted renderer and poll branches; verify browser-supplied frame provenance, revocation, wrong/nested/destroyed frames and independent failing callbacks. Run tests/app-ready-client.test.mjs for admitted-before-settlement and recovery details. These are source-executing VM fixtures, not live routed-runtime or browser proof; real installed-app browser/update acceptance remains required.

features.description: Chats retains exact projected row fields across unrelated owner writes and reflects row-affecting writes on main, host-profile, container and restricted runtimes; main reuses quiet head rows.
features.how_to_test: Seed a completed synthetic thread, compare list rows before and after eight owner read-state writes, require main head reuse without fallback, then rename through the exact runtime route and assert the changed title updates. Host-profile uses its profile API; restricted uses its mode-0600 ingress socket. Fixture evidence only, not live runtime/browser acceptance.

features.description: Temporary private-agent chats never enter ordinary stores; standard agents are explicitly refused. This matrix fixture proves the privacy policy, not real-container or confidential-model operation.
features.how_to_test: Assert the real Service refuses Incognito on the standard agent of each runtime kind with 409 incognito_private_only before upstream admission; use the dedicated synthetic private browser/stock rig for positive no-persistence proof.

features.description: Stock local fact_store and prefetch recall survive process/container restart in each runtime's own Hermes home without crossing agent/profile homes.
features.how_to_test: Run tests/holographic_container_proof.py on an isolated Docker worker. Real stock gateway containers model main-home, named-profile, managed-container and restricted-home scopes; the stock memory initializer must inject fact_store/fact_feedback, add/search/prefetch a canary, restart only its disposable gateway and recall again for every kind. Restricted proof also backs up via native SQLite-safe backup, imports into a second home, applies Wizard import wiring, and recalls. This is stock runtime home/tool behavior, not live Wizard routing or model adherence. Never use existing private agents or owner homes. The Holographic memory workflow saves the per-kind JSON results; an empty report or failed command fails CI.

features.description: Owner-scoped Hermes-only owned follow-up processing without imposed style instructions; routed kinds retain done state and admission behavior.
features.how_to_test: Admit a synthetic HTTP turn per kind and inspect actual upstream instructions: no runtime receives OWNED_OPEN_WORK_INSTRUCTIONS, because reply and follow-up style belong to its persona. Project an owned Still open reply through the real session list, assert routed kinds stay done without owned_work or automatic sends, and execute the Hermes guard. tests/owned-open-work.test.ts additionally proves the main service's hidden continuation, restart dedupe and exact optional-handle behavior. These are disposable fixture checks, not live-model or browser proof.

features.description: A failed run names why it failed on the thread row (wizard_last_run_error on full rows, runError on compact list rows): provider_auth, provider_billing, provider_quota, network or unknown, with the provider route and the provider's own words. wizard-ux shows it behind the off-by-default wizard/failure-reason tweak.
features.how_to_test: Fail a real HTTP admission on the openai-codex route with a synthetic HTTP 402 plan-ended error, read the run, then list the thread in the full and ?view=list shapes on main, host-profile, container and restricted. Require code provider_billing, provider openai-codex and the provider's words. Synthetic HTTP fixture evidence, not live provider proof.

features.description: A reply Hermes accepted but refused with runtime_draining because the gateway began a restart is sent again by itself once (same words, same thread), with no Retry; reading it again never sends a duplicate.
features.how_to_test: Admit a real HTTP run, make the fixture Hermes fail it with error runtime_draining, then read the run on main, host-profile, container and restricted. Require exactly one automatic resend carrying the owner's words and no further sends on later reads. Synthetic HTTP fixture evidence, not a live gateway restart.

features.description: A diagnosed expired sign-in waits for an observed unavailable-to-ready transition and resends the saved request once on the same locked model route; a stale picker retry on another model is refused, not misacknowledged or duplicated.
features.how_to_test: Fail a real HTTP admission with a controlled zero-token sign-in error, observe unavailable then ready, and assert one same-model source-preserving resend on main, host-profile, container and restricted queues.

features.description: Every runtime receives the Supervisor spell and six Hermes session-injected tools; standard agents can report through their authenticated transport. Scheduled replies share Reporter validation.
features.how_to_test: Admit an ordinary run per kind; inspect shared spell, install asset bundle into disposable homes, call report through main loopback or per-agent credential/socket, check service-derived identity and queued review. Verify private/siloed refusal separately before ledger reads.
features.privacy_seal_exemption: Private and siloed agents refuse all Supervisor tools without sharing. Covered by tests/supervisor.test.ts and per-routed-kind refusal assertions; no standard runtime kind is exempt.

features.description: Reject self-identified agent-to-agent run/chat/steer writes into existing owner threads before runtime side effects; preserve ordinary sends.
features.how_to_test: For every runtime kind, POST agent-to-agent prefix and NOT-a-James-message inputs through run, steer, chat and chat/stream. Require HTTP 409 agent_to_agent_thread_write and no upstream writes, then accept a normal owner run and a Supervisor update that quotes the marker below its first line, and list sessions.

features.description: All agent kinds receive only WizardOS facts, the persona pointer and the status protocol, never a reply-style rule, whatever response_style an older shell saved. The Markdown fact overrides only the API-server plain-text line, so the runtime's own keep-replies-brief default survives.
features.how_to_test: Admit fresh-install and legacy summary/concise/own turns through main, host-profile, container and restricted HTTP routes; assert settings read Own and actual upstream instructions contain Wizard facts, the persona pointer and STATUS_PROTOCOL_INSTRUCTIONS without reply-style rules, and with the scoped Markdown override that keeps the runtime's brevity default. Fixture proof covers prompt delivery, not model compliance.

features.description: The optional signed Android companion preserves each routed reply while asynchronously stopping and parking its native recording.
features.how_to_test: In wizard-ux run node --test tests/shell-recording-routes.test.mjs. The real parkReply function runs for main, host-profile, container and restricted routes with asynchronous shell and synchronous full-app recorders; it preserves session, agent, typed draft and audio, and acknowledges only after durable held custody. Meeting cancellation also awaits native bytes before acknowledgement. This is synthetic source-executed evidence, not live provider or physical-phone proof. Companion UX PR: humanitylabs-org/wizard-ux#504.

features.description: Agent-owned thread collections persist independently of agent runtime kind and hydrate all visible members outside global archive windows
features.how_to_test: Authenticate as each main/host-profile/container/restricted agent (restricted via its Unix gateway), list/search/create/add/remove/delete own Spaces (spaces_add and full PUT snapshots keep a chat in one Space per agent), refuse foreign Spaces as not_found, project assistant-only subject metadata, file by status-line space, restart and verify durable membership. Managed-container startup upgrades are covered in tests/managed-harness-upgrade.test.ts. In wizard-ux, qa-chats-focus.cjs pickerAcceptance verifies main and routed New Space fills use the scoped Spaces tool instruction (never a main-only CLI), exactly once through the normal outbox with the selected agent. In wizard-ux, node --test tests/space-members.test.mjs checks missing-member hydration for main, host-profile, container and restricted routes, scope changes, hidden/private discovery, 500 members and bounded polling. QA_SPACE_MEMBERS_ONLY=1 node qa-chats-focus.cjs <origin> verifies phone/desktop Focus shows 82 visible members with 62 archived beyond the global archive-50, keeps All windowed and preserves Back. These are fixture/browser checks, not live runtime proof.

features.description: Deliver the cold-readable, situation-first Ready ask contract to every runtime kind
features.how_to_test: Admit a real HTTP run for main, host-profile, container and restricted fixtures; capture the instructions at the routed upstream boundary and assert the complete shared status contract, 140-character limit, situation then action, reply-word meaning and jargon ban, including the rule that an unbuilt plan/diagnosis/audit/proposal for requested work must either start in the same turn with fyi and a verified running mechanism or ask needs_you with a reply word that starts it; only explicitly research-only or hypothetical requests may finish at the plan. Round-trip a compliant synthetic needs_you answer through the Ready list and history, preserving the ask while hiding its marker. This proves prompt delivery and projection, not stochastic model adherence or live-provider behavior.

features.description: Emit needs_you/done/working status with ask, subject and title
features.how_to_test: Project ask, subject and title without raw tags. tests/open-ask.node.mjs covers Ready/Working cases and real HTTP lists on main, host-profile, container and restricted: an unanswered needs_you ask survives progress while background continues, with wizard_background preserved in slim lists; immediate QR actions stay Ready even when their explanation says it will link the phone, while future delivery promises stay Working. A queued owner message (not yet in the transcript) or an admitted started/accepted/running/unknown run keeps its lifecycle ahead of an older transcript ask and helper background: queued input drops every transcript ask, a running run keeps only asks its own replies wrote after admission, and helper-only rows without a run id still yield to owner gates. tests/heavy-status.test.ts exercises real list and notice delivery routes for all four runtime kinds: check stays Working until heavy results land; done is not demoted and never creates an open ask. On upgrade, legacy terminal jobs are acknowledged once, preserve done/check, and never inject stale sibling notices; post-migration results remain owed across reopens until delivery. Companion wizard-ux tests/ready-open-ask.test.mjs verifies the muted Helper still working badge and latest helper-reply preview. Fixture/unit evidence is not browser, two-skin visual or live-model acceptance.

features.description: A thread leaves Working as soon as its run finishes, not when the cached listing expires
features.how_to_test: Admit a run, make the list read Hermes while the run is live, finish the run and read its status as the browser does, then list again: the thread must stop listing as Working within 1 s, well inside main's 30 s cached Hermes listing, and its row must come from the finished listing (two messages). Main runs the direct admission path (fails without the re-read) and the durable-queue path on a fresh-mode box without state.db (fails unless the queue revision re-reads the listing: the row must come from the finished listing too); host-profile, container and restricted list live through their agent and are asserted the same way. tests/list-working-after-reply.node.mjs also covers a listing read already in flight when a direct or queued run ends, and a new queued chat the listing skipped until its reply. Fixture HTTP evidence only, not browser or live-model acceptance.

features.description: Connecting a provider never attaches it to the main agent: with WIZARD_MAIN_PROVIDER_ATTACH on, the main agent's picker lists only attached providers (the configured one first), a model change onto an unattached provider is refused before Hermes, and the owner attaches providers explicitly. Main lists only the attached configured provider and answers 409 provider_not_attached; routed kinds keep their single own-provider row, no attach fields, and 409 model_not_allowed. No refused change reaches any Hermes, and an allowed model change still succeeds. tests/main-provider-attach.test.ts covers the switch off, attach/detach and the pool. Synthetic HTTP fixture evidence, not live box proof.

features.description: The built-in file store keeps every upload findable by id: after more than 5,000 later uploads the first attachment still opens, still resolves for the agent and is still found as a duplicate; opening it never rewrites the index.

features.description: A live reply resumes by seq after a dropped stream: no doubled words, offline waits for the network, a replay gap drops the partial text, never a second admission
features.how_to_test: Run QA_GROUP=resume QA_KINDS=main,host-profile,container,restricted QA_UX_ROOT=<ux> QA_OUT=<fresh-output> QA_EXTERNAL_ROOT=<worker-root> node qa/agent-parity/browser.mjs (Linux also needs QA_CHROMIUM=<chrome> QA_PLAYWRIGHT=<playwright>). Per kind, the real shell sends one turn through the real Service; the synthetic runtime streams numbered frames (GET /v1/runs/<id>/events replays from the oldest retained frame; a model-locked turn's chat/stream is numbered and replayed by the Service's locked-run bridge). Every Service connection is cut mid-reply: the next read replays and the live bubble shows each word once. Offline, no stream read happens until the browser is back online, then it resumes at once. A replay that lost frames (past the 4000-frame retention, replay.truncated) drops the partial text and the transcript answer shows once. One admission throughout. Synthetic-runtime browser evidence, not live provider acceptance.

features.description: After one online visit the shell opens offline from its scoped worker copy; main threads show this device's saved copy, labelled; routed threads are never stored; no /wizard/* response is cached
features.how_to_test: Run QA_GROUP=offline QA_KINDS=main,host-profile,container,restricted QA_UX_ROOT=<ux> QA_OUT=<fresh-output> QA_EXTERNAL_ROOT=<worker-root> node qa/agent-parity/browser.mjs (Linux also needs QA_CHROMIUM=<chrome> QA_PLAYWRIGHT=<playwright>). Per kind, with service workers allowed: open the thread online, wait for the scoped worker to hold the shell (wos-shell-v1 has the page, live.js and chats.js), assert no cache entry under /wizard/ (APIs, attachments, files), then reload with the browser offline. The shell boots from the worker copy. Main: the thread paints this device's saved copy with its Saved copy label. Routed kinds: the thread was never written to the wos-thread-cache store and its words appear nowhere offline. Back online the shell reconnects. Release replacement (one release at a time) is kind-independent and covered by wizard-ux/tests/shell-offline-sw.test.mjs.

features.how_to_test: Load bounded newest/oldest history pages and search an older thread; assert no omissions or duplicate boundaries. For each agent kind, render the real chat list: empty Yesterday/Past week sections are absent, populated historical sections remain available.

features.description: Each agent learns its own app jobs and receives app-first, source-of-truth, explicit tool-error reporting and registered-exact-tool-name rules; main pointer skills load the app's shipped skill first.
features.how_to_test: Install a synthetic app with a provides job and shipped skill into the real Service's apps.json, restart, and initialize its wizard MCP gateway through each main, host-profile, container and restricted agent's own credential and transport (restricted: Unix socket). Assert exact new app-first and source-of-truth lines, including missing-tool search/retry, no old-chat guesses or app URLs, checked negative results and explicit tool-error reporting; assert registered exact tool names and absence of the old speculative-name instruction. Repeat after uninstall to prove the standalone rules survive without apps. Main pointer skills load the shipped skill with skill_view first; other kinds receive their own inline job map and no pointer wording. Uninstall removes the pointer and app name. These execute actual Service gateway handlers against disposable synthetic upstreams, not stock live Hermes, model adherence or browser acceptance. Full fixture execution must be recorded separately; main live-model pointer proof is ops/acceptance/pointer-skills (fresh KVM VM).

features.description: Verify standard credentials cannot enumerate/open/search private threads
features.how_to_test: Verify standard credentials cannot enumerate/open/search private threads; own-agent principal cannot use owner attachment ids. Metadata only on existing agents.

Verify Opus remains immutable, then restart/replay without duplication and confirm picker edits do not admit chat turns. Main fixture persists browser_model_lock in synthetic SQLite. An earlier live bridge override fails this queued-admission regression; shared main already preserves it and must not adopt that override. Undeclared models remain forbidden by existing model_not_allowed tests. Fixture-only, not real-provider acceptance.

These are fixture checks, not live runtime proof.

features.description: A legacy Claude Code default starts new main chats on the ready Claude pool's same model; routed agents and explicit picks keep their own route

features.description: A three-line mobile draft keeps every editing row selectable and Send reachable without the model control intercepting either target

For each route, open its New chat through the supported shell path, enter a three-line draft, select the lower lines, and use elementFromPoint to require the second-last row to hit the textarea and Send to hit the Send button. The full matrix also covers phone/native widths 360 and 412, Nebula and Grove, plus native landscape. All requests are locally fixtured; foreign origins and agent-message writes fail the run. features.how_to_test: Compact an isolated long fixture thread; reload visible history and continue without leaking memory scaffolding or losing attachments.

Remove the app grant and run again: the same thread is unhidden, fallback is recorded and no notification is sent. Restricted uses a mode-0600 Unix ingress; host-profile uses /p/parity-profile.

features.description: Stop shows the moment a message is sent; before the run exists it withdraws the pending send (no run admitted), after that it stops the exact run from the receipt
features.how_to_test: In wizard-ux run node --test tests/stop-before-run.test.mjs. The real outbox runs against a local HTTP boundary: Stop during upload, server transcription or offline waiting creates zero /v1/runs calls and keeps the recording; Stop while the run POST is in flight resolves with the receipt's run id; a steer in flight that is rejected after Stop never becomes a new turn. The real LIVE.cancelSend block runs for main, host-profile, container and restricted threads and withdraws only that thread's sends and stops only its own run (including a reply queued to steer the live run, and a slow phone take arriving after the tap hold). This is synthetic source-executed evidence; fenced browser QA on a scratch shell is reported separately. Companion UX PR: humanitylabs-org/wizard-ux#649.

Synthetic source-executed evidence; live two-browser check recorded on humanitylabs-org/wizard-ux#670.

features.how_to_test: In wizard-ux run node --test tests/chat-tweak-card.test.mjs: the same history and list rows for main, host-profile, container and restricted threads parse to the same tweak ids, render the same switch card bound to current WosExperience state, and strip the marker from the full-list preview; a tap toggles the device's Look once. In this repo tests/session-list-view.node.mjs proves the slim Chats list preview strips the marker (complete and cut off) for all four kinds. The Service passes the marker through history unchanged for every kind. Synthetic source-executed evidence; browser cells in wizard-ux/tests/qa-chat-tweak-card.cjs.

features.description: Shared Chats lists (Spaces and their members, subject order, pins) keep every device's and agent's change for main and routed threads: edits are item operations applied atomically by the service, never a device's whole cached list, so a stale or simultaneous device cannot drop another's edit.
features.how_to_test: In wizard-agent-service, npx vitest run tests/ui-preferences.test.ts covers PATCH item operations (concurrent devices on one list, idempotency, gone Space no-op, 400 without writing, PUT kept for older shells). In wizard-ux, node --test tests/synced-lists.test.mjs runs every synced list key through tests/two-devices.mjs (stale device and GET,GET,PUT,PUT race, with and without PATCH support) for main, host-profile, container and restricted thread ids. Synthetic source-executed evidence; live two-browser check recorded on the wizard-ux PR.

The call is not refused; with the app off the call returns '<agent> is not allowed to use Synthetic Video. The owner can turn it on in Connections.' and tools/list has none of its tools; back on, the call is not refused, with no restart. tests/agents-sealed-apps.test.ts covers the owner API path, the private-app seal and new-agent defaults. Host-profile, container and restricted agents' Chats windows open beside it keep their own threads and lists untouched.
features.how_to_test: In wizard-ux, node --test tests/ai-apps-agent-parity.test.mjs runs the real phone (web/app.js) and desktop (web/desktop/desktop.js) adapter code with a main, host-profile, container and restricted Chats window open (a routed one in front): the drawer lists only the main agent's rows, its interrupted, Yesterday and Past week chats included in Ready, and done, snooze and rename on each of them land on the main window once with no routed window touched. Synthetic source-executed evidence; write-free browser checks recorded on wizard-ux PR #888; missing-bucket fix on wizard-ux PR #961.

features.description: An owner's ChatGPT/Claude/Hermes export dropped in Files is archived as searchable chats in the owner's Files, and picked Hermes skills install only into the importing agent's own home, or, from the Importer app, into another WizardOS agent the owner picks (dest: a standard container or host profile agent; restricted agents are never offered).
features.how_to_test: For every runtime kind, upload a synthetic ChatGPT export and a synthetic Hermes backup through the Service's Files upload, run the wizard-os bring_data tool with that kind's own HERMES_HOME and the owner Files root, then assert scan counts, the archived chat under Files/Imported/ChatGPT, the scan record and the installed skill under that agent's home only, and that no credential from the export appears in tool output. Synthetic fixture evidence, not live/browser evidence.

features.description: Green all-done reply groups acknowledge after continuous visible/front-thread dwell or an owner send that snapshots their exact loaded server id/updated_at versions, separately for each agent/thread scope. Ordinary-height replies require their top or at least 40 percent visible; only replies taller than the readable viewport permit a small visible tail. Amber stays untouched by auto-Seen and send-clear; explicit Dismiss acknowledges amber groups via exact per-id versions and the existing Ready Done operation. Blocked and running rows have no Dismiss. The strip stays visible for running, needs-you, blocked or finished-but-unseen groups; only acknowledged-only or empty threads have no strip. Header counts active groups only as N open; acknowledged history remains a collapsed footer. Sends/steers paint before navigation, commit Seen only after durable Outbox custody and cancel on save refusal. Late ledger reads cannot expand the version snapshot. Away shares never acknowledge. Ordinary phone browsers require focus; only native phone bridges use the no-focus exception. Dropdown expansion is not seeing. Tracker header/list form one opaque panel; opening and anchored jumps leave the first line below the measured strip, with tweak-off eye-line unchanged. New clients send both legacy ids and versioned items; the prepared service compares each id/updated_at inside its synchronous atomic store write and returns acknowledged or stale, preserving ids-only behavior for old clients. Stale responses retire optimistic pins and remain unseen. The UX works with the old endpoint, but atomic server rejection requires deploying the prepared service separately.
features.how_to_test: Run wizard-ux tests/thread-tracker-autoseen.test.mjs for main, host-profile, container and restricted scoped-client GET/Seen payloads, running-only strip presence, remaining-running presence after Seen, acknowledged-only absence and no cross-agent leakage. With client clock -60s, aligned and +60s, acknowledge the same already-loaded all-done versions but never a completion arriving 10s after send, a changed member version or an unpinned late-ledger id. Reload a changed version while durable custody waits: it must receive no Seen POST. A 300px reply with a 50px tail held 1s must not acknowledge; a 4000px reply tail held 1s must. Include tests/thread-tracker-send.test.mjs for send/steer before-navigation scoping, deferred commit/cancel, storage refusal and away-share exclusion; sync tests cover refusal rollback and late-ledger non-expansion. Require late streamed anchors to re-arm without a render, native-phone no-focus acceptance versus ordinary-browser focus refusal, and 1 amber plus 3 acknowledged reading 1 open. Run wizard-ux tools/qa-thread-tracker.cjs on the admitted browser worker for phone, Android document-scroll and AI-apps desktop in Nebula/Grove. Measure geometry continuously throughout dwell, not just before queued shell repaints. Require hidden/background refusal, later unseen re-arm, measured first-line clearance, opaque seam and unchanged tweak-off eye-line; all service writes intercepted. These are synthetic client/browser evidence, not live routed runtime-transport or physical-device proof. The server thread-tracker fixture covers old/new-client CAS, standalone amber dismissal, newer-version rearm and actual upstream action-text instructions for all runtime kinds. UX tests additionally require same-frame last-amber/Ready Done paint and rollback on stale Seen, not a new attention store. These are fixture HTTP checks rather than physical-device or live model-adherence proof.

features.description: Only with the owner's Thread tracker tweak on, Seen accepts exact per-id versions atomically, reports stale without acknowledging newer unseen replies, and keeps legacy ids-only requests. Explicit amber Dismiss uses Seen, including non-try asks; newer action text reopens it. Optional ask/summary text is bounded and preserved. Every runtime receives the rule that needs_you requires one specific owner action named in title/ask and optional follow-ups are done. Every runtime receives the mandatory every-ask instruction, including answered questions as done and mid-turn additions. The 16-item reply cap prioritizes open asks on overflow; earlier answered asks need not repeat. Retention evicts seen done, then unseen done asks, never unresolved work. Separate asks stay recorded per id, but counts group by current reply anchor using the most urgent member; Seen of every member acknowledges that reply. Unknown anchors stay separate. The status line never shows in the transcript, and a quote reply tells the agent which message and ask it answers. With the tweak off the ledger answers empty, nothing is recorded and the quote reaches the agent unchanged. Routed runs that finish while the thread is closed are ingested from their run read. Main builder agent only: every other agent gets no instructions, no ingestion and an empty ledger, its stored rows kept.
features.how_to_test: Main builder agent only (James, 9 Nov 2026): for host-profile, container and restricted HTTP fixtures with the tweak on, assert no tracker/items instructions, no counts/items, Seen no-op and no ingestion of a finished run; stored rows of other agents stay untouched. For the main HTTP fixture, inspect actual upstream run instructions: require the complete mandatory every-ask contract, quick answered question = done, mid-turn additions, 16-item cap and open-first overflow without repeating earlier answers. Read a transcript whose assistant reply carries items: assert no items text in history, one most-urgent count for two asks on one reply, both per-id ledger items anchored to the reply, partial Seen remains actionable, all-member Seen persists as one acknowledged reply, and the runtime input carries the plain reply-to sentence. With the tweak false and absent in separate scenes, assert no tracker/items instructions, empty counts/items, Seen no-op and unchanged quote. tests/thread-items.test.ts executes these same per-kind checks plus 16-item parse/normalization and retention/restart regressions (seen done before unseen done, open states survive quick-answer churn, soft limit if all asks are open). Synthetic HTTP fixture evidence only, not model compliance, live runtime, browser or physical-phone proof.

features.description: Look up in the Chats selection menu explains selected words with a fast stateless model (claude-haiku-4-5, no tools, no history) in the context of their own message only, identically for main, host-profile, container and restricted agents; private agents, private threads and Incognito never reach a cloud model, decided from the session's pinned agent on the server, not the caller's agent field.
features.how_to_test: Server: tests/lookup.node.mjs (contract, stream shape, 400/413/415, 800-char bound, model identity, no persistence) and tests/lookup-privacy.test.ts (private agent's pinned session refused with agent omitted, spoofed as main/hermes or explicit, zero broker calls; a standard thread explained). UX (wizard-ux PR #1181): tests/lookup-scope-parity.test.mjs runs the real lookupScope for main, host-profile, container and restricted windows plus private agent/thread/Incognito/private default/vanished window; tests/lookup-pop.browser.cjs covers popover behaviour in real Chromium on a synthetic thread. Synthetic fixture evidence, not a real Android long-press or real routed-agent live run.

features.description: A turn that handed off to a detached background job (a deploy started through wizard_restart_report.py) keeps its chat in Working, never Ready or Stuck, until the job reports; returned helpers read as waiting on a background job with no Resume.
features.how_to_test: Through real synthetic HTTP lists (full and slim) on main, host-profile, container and restricted Unix ingress: a done reply with a live deploy receipt is Working; the same thread settles once the receipt reports. Disposable receipts in a scene temp dir; no live deploy, owner write or browser proof. tests/detached-job-wait.test.ts covers the receipt reader, its age bounds and the stuck-vs-background helper phase.
